Take on an empty stomach (1 h before or 2 h after food) for reliable absorption
Use caution; consider dose reduction in severe impairment
Caution; reduce dose in significant hepatic impairment

summary: Chlorambucil is an orally active aromatic nitrogen mustard alkylating agent used as palliative therapy for chronic lymphocytic (lymphatic) leukemia, malignant lymphomas (including lymphosarcoma and giant follicular lymphoma), and Hodgkin's disease. Usual dose is 0.1-0.2 mg/kg/day for 3-6 weeks, adjusted to blood counts. It carries a boxed warning for severe bone marrow suppression, human carcinogenicity, probable mutagenicity/teratogenicity, and infertility. It is not curative but can produce useful palliation.
indications: Malignant lymphomas including lymphosarcoma and giant follicular lymphoma

dosage.d: 0.1-0.2 mg/kg body weight daily (about 4-10 mg/day for the average patient)
dosage.t: Once daily for 3-6 weeks; full daily dose may be given at one time
dosage.n: Reduce as soon as white cell count falls abruptly
When marrow infiltrated or hypoplastic, do not exceed 0.1 mg/kg (~6 mg) daily

dosage.d: Initial single dose 0.4 mg/kg, increased by 0.1 mg/kg per pulse until lymphocytosis controlled or toxicity
dosage.n: Subsequent doses modified to produce mild hematologic toxicity

admin: Administer orally as a single daily dose; preferably on an empty stomach
Obtain baseline and at least weekly complete blood counts during therapy
Reduce or interrupt dose with abrupt fall in white cells or platelets
Handle as a hazardous cytotoxic drug; avoid skin contact and crushing tablets
Maintain hydration; manage nausea with antiemetics as needed
moa: Chlorambucil is an aromatic nitrogen mustard derivative that acts as a bifunctional alkylating agent. It forms reactive ethyleneimonium intermediates that crosslink and alkylate DNA, interfering with DNA replication and transcription. The resulting DNA damage induces cellular apoptosis via accumulation of cytosolic p53 and subsequent activation of the pro-apoptotic protein Bax. It is cell-cycle non-specific and is particularly active against lymphoid tissue.

absolute: Prior demonstrated resistance of the disease to chlorambucil
relative: Possible cross-hypersensitivity (skin rash) with other alkylating agents
Recent radiotherapy or cytotoxic chemotherapy within prior 4 weeks
History of seizures or head trauma (lowered seizure threshold)
monitor: Complete blood count with differential and platelets (at least weekly)

preg: Contraindicated. Chlorambucil can cause fetal harm; unilateral renal agenesis has been reported in offspring exposed in the first trimester, and urogenital malformations occur in animals. Women of childbearing potential should avoid pregnancy and use effective contraception; men should be counseled on infertility/genotoxic risk.
lact: It is not known whether chlorambucil is excreted in human milk. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in a nursing infant, either discontinue nursing or discontinue the drug.
renal: Use with caution; patients with renal impairment may be at increased risk of myelosuppression. Consider dose reduction in severe renal impairment and monitor counts closely.
hepatic: Caution in significant hepatic impairment; dose reduction may be required as chlorambucil is hepatically metabolized. Monitor liver function.

major: Live vaccines - risk of severe/fatal infection in immunosuppressed patients; avoid
Other myelosuppressive chemotherapy or radiotherapy - additive marrow toxicity
moderate: Other immunosuppressants - additive immunosuppression and infection risk
Drugs lowering seizure threshold - additive risk of seizures
minor: Phenylbutazone - reported to enhance chlorambucil toxicity; reduce dose
interactions.food: Food reduces and delays absorption; take on an empty stomach (1 hour before or 2 hours after meals).
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol; it can worsen nausea and add to hepatic burden.
interactions.diagnostics: Causes leukopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia and anemia; may elevate liver enzymes and uric acid.

common: Bone marrow suppression (leukopenia, neutropenia, thrombocytopenia, anemia)
serious: Severe and sometimes irreversible bone marrow failure / pancytopenia
Seizures (especially in children with nephrotic syndrome and at high/cumulative doses)
rare: Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis
Severe skin reactions / drug reaction with eosinophilia

monitoring: Complete blood count with differential and platelets at least weekly
counsel: This is a strong cancer medicine - take exactly as prescribed, ideally on an empty stomach
Regular blood tests are essential to check your blood counts
Report fever, sore throat, unusual bruising or bleeding, or signs of infection promptly
Use effective contraception; the drug can harm an unborn baby and may cause infertility
Tell your doctor about any fits/seizures, severe rash, or breathing problems
pk: Hematologic effects develop over days to weeks of dosing
Rapidly and almost completely absorbed; peak plasma ~1 hour
Parent ~1.5 h; active metabolite phenylacetic acid mustard ~2.5 h
Extensively metabolized; little unchanged drug excreted in urine
Refrigerate at 2-8 C; protect from light
pearls: BOXED WARNING: severe bone marrow suppression; human carcinogen; probably mutagenic and teratogenic; causes infertility
Adjust dose to blood counts - reduce promptly when WBC falls abruptly
Children with nephrotic syndrome are at particular risk of seizures
Not curative - aim is palliation in CLL, lymphomas and Hodgkin's disease
Avoid live vaccines and minimize infection exposure during therapy
missed: If a dose is missed, contact the prescriber for advice rather than doubling up. Do not take two doses together; consistent dosing relative to blood counts is important.
overdose: Main effect is reversible pancytopenia; neurologic toxicity ranging from agitation and ataxia to multiple grand mal seizures has occurred. There is no known antidote and chlorambucil is not dialyzable. Monitor the blood picture closely, give supportive care and blood transfusions as needed, and treat seizures.
